differences.title: 1. EXECUTION LOCATION
differences.leftDesc: Components rendered on the server, reducing client-side load and improving initial render.
differences.rightDesc: Components rendered in the user's browser, enabling interactivity and dynamic updates.

differences.title: 2. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Less JavaScript sent to the client, leading to quicker perceived performance.
differences.rightDesc: More JavaScript bundled and sent, potentially delaying interactivity.

differences.title: 3. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Suitable for static content or data fetching; direct event handling is limited.
differences.rightDesc: Ideal for interactive UIs, user input, and real-time updates.

differences.title: 4. DATA ACCESS
differences.leftDesc: Can directly access server resources like databases without extra network hops.
differences.rightDesc: Requires API calls to fetch data from the server.

differences.title: 5. SEO
differences.leftDesc: Content is fully rendered server-side, making it easily crawlable by search engines.
differences.rightDesc: SEO is good but relies on JavaScript execution by crawlers.

differences.title: 6. CODE SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Less JavaScript payload sent to the client, improving performance on slower networks.
differences.rightDesc: More JavaScript required for client rendering, potentially increasing bundle size.

differences.title: 7. SECURITY
differences.leftDesc: Sensitive logic or API keys can be kept on the server, reducing exposure.
differences.rightDesc: Client-side code is visible, requiring careful handling of sensitive information.
